question.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Involving Sine with Non-Special Angles
question.problem: Calculate, in degrees, rounded to the nearest integer, the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{2}{3}$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{2}{3})=41.810{…}^{∘}≈{41.81}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${41.81}^{∘}$ lies inside the range, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={41.81}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={41.81}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the second quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={41.81}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977985/assets/bc0c031fe6ccbb40dc77474582b301456f537ee2a649ba2d5b3bca9b1240618f.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{41.81}^{∘} \\  & ={138.19}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions (rounded to the nearest integer) are $x={42}^{∘},{138}^{∘}.$
